previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, diabetes, and pseudoseizures was admitted after an episode of syncope associated with severe abdominal pain radiating to the left testicle, nausea, vomiting, and chest tightness. He had been unable to eat for three days and reported seeing blood and 'soot' in his vomit. In the ED, he had tachycardia and an elevated lactate of 7.2 with an anion gap of 24, which normalized after IV fluids. Workup ruled out myocardial infarction with normal troponins and EKG, and no arrhythmias on telemetry. The syncope was attributed to vagal episodes triggered by pain. He was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, pain control, and antiemetics. By hospital day two, his symptoms improved, he tolerated clear liquids, and was transitioned to oral medications. He was discharged home with improved pain, instructions to restart metformin, new prescription for ondansetron, and follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ yo M with chronic pancreatitis, PTSD, bipolar 
disorder, seizure vs. pseudoseizure disorder, DM2, and HTN who 
presents with 2 days of continuing abdominal pain and syncope 
since his recent hospital discharge.
.
# Abdominal pain, nausea: Likely chronic pancreatitis and 
psychiatric distress. No acute process evident on labs or 
imaging. LFTs and lipase normal. Urine and serum tox screens 
negative. We gave him IVF and kept him NPO for the first morning 
while he was here, but he soon demanded to eat. We thus 
transitioned him from IV dilaudid to PO dialudid and he 
tolerated clears well. His pain was very well-controlled and he 
desired to eat regular food so we advanced his diet. We gave him 
Zofran PRN. 
.
On hospital day 2, he wanted to be discharged so he could see 
his children (who he had not seen for 5 months) for Father's 
Day. He stated that his pain was very well-controlled. Since he 
was tolerating regular food with minimal abdominal pain and no 
n/v, we discharged him.
.
# Syncope: Has had previous extensive evaluations. He was not 
orthostatic. Likely vasovagal from pain + psychiatric. We gave 
him IVF and controlled his pain with IV and then PO dilaudid.
.
# PTSD, bipolar disorder: Patient asked to see psychiatrist. He 
is having nightmares and is in distress, but he is not an acute 
danger to himself or others as he denies HI/SI.  He is also 
stressed about not being able to pay his bills. Psychiatry saw 
him and recommended restarting ziprasidone, gabapentin, and 
prazosin (which apparently has been shown to decrease 
nightmares). They also recommended stopping amitriptyline as it 
may contribute to orthostasis. He has an intake appointment 
scheduled with Community Counseling on ___. Records of his 
previous inpatient stay on ___ 4 were given to him in a 
sealed envelope for him to bring to his care providers at 
___ Counseling. Social work did not have a chance to see 
him before he was discharged. 
.
He will need further management of his psychiatric medications 
as an outpatient. Psych consult here felt that starting an SSRI 
for management of his depression and anxiety may be beneficial, 
though caution should be exercised given possibility of 
triggering mania. Psych consult also questioned the use of 
ziprasidone given its metabolic side effects. 
.
# Seizure vs. pseudoseizure: Pseudoseizure but not seizure 
activity witnessed the morning after his nighttime admission.  
When seen by psychiatry, it was recommended that he be ruled out 
for conversion disorder (non-electrical seizures).
.
# GERD: Continued home omeprazole.
.
# HTN: Continued home lisinopril.
.
# Diabetes: Metformin was held while he was NPO, restarted on 
discharge.
.
# Anemia and thrombocytosis: Chronic and stable.

FINDINGS:  The heart and mediastinal contours appear unremarkable.  The hila

are grossly intact.  No subdiaphragmatic free air is noted.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process; no evidence of free air.

HISTORY:  ___ male with altered mental status.

STUDY:  CT of the head without contrast.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  There is no intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, edema, or large
territorial infarct.  Gray-white differentiation is preserved.  Ventricles and
sulci appear prominent for the patient's age.  The sinuses and air cells are
well-pneumatized.  Bony structures are intact.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial process; atrophic changes.

HISTORY:  ___ male with acute on chronic abdominal pain in the
epigastric and left lower quadrant regions.

STUDY:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast; coronal and sagittal
reformatted images were also generated.

FINDINGS:

ABDOMEN:  The visualized portion of the heart and lungs appear unremarkable.

The liver demonstrates no focal lesion or biliary dilatation.  Clips in the
gallbladder fossa are consistent with prior cholecystectomy.  The spleen is
normal in size and appearance.  Multiple calcifications are noted throughout
an elongated atrophic pancreas consistent with chronic pancreatitis.  The
adrenal glands are normal appearing bilaterally.  The kidneys enhance with and
excrete contrast symmetrically.  The small intestine shows no evidence of
obstruction.  The colon shows no evidence of wall thickening or obstruction. 
The aorta, IVC, portal vein and their major branches all appear patent.  No
lymphadenopathy is seen.  No free air or free fluid is noted.

PELVIS:  Bladder, prostate, and rectum appear unremarkable.  The appendix is
seen and is normal.  Scant diverticulosis is noted throughout the sigmoid
colon without evidence of diverticulitis.

BONES:  No aggressive lytic or sclerotic lesions are seen.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Pancreatic calcifications consistent with chronic pancreatitis.
2.  Status post cholecystectomy.
3.  No evidence of bowel obstruction.
